clue.text: Graph to once again take advantage of color

blocks.note: a graph is a chart

blocks.clueFragment: to once again take advantage of
blocks.note: to use again: RE- (again) plus USE (take advantage of)

explanation.surface: Someone redraws a chart purely to exploit a colour scheme a second time.
explanation.definitionFit: Chartreuse is a yellowish-green shade named after the liqueur.

clue.text: Loudly sing like Bing Crosby, formerly, with more sodden knitwear

indicators.note: loudly says the words are to be heard aloud and judged by sound

blocks.note: Bing Crosby was the archetypal crooner
ex means former, as in ex-wife
comparative of wet

explanation.surface: An old-style singer belts out a tune while his woollens grow ever soggier.
explanation.walkthrough: Said in one breath, croon-ex-wetter runs together as crew-neck sweater.
explanation.definitionFit: A crew-neck sweater is a pullover with a round, close-fitting neckline, a standard item of knitwear.

clue.text: Cheat as red alert swirls around university

indicators.note: letters that swirl are churned round into a new order
around wraps the churned letters about the next piece

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged
U is the standard abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: A cheat is caught as alarms go off across a campus.
explanation.definitionFit: An adulterer cheats on a spouse, so 'cheat' in the marital sense names one.

clue.text: Losing one's composure, drink a round

blocks.note: tea is a drink
a ring is a round shape

explanation.surface: Someone getting flustered decides to buy a round of drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A round' suggests buying drinks for everyone; here it is a circle.
explanation.definitionFit: Tearing up, starting to cry, is a sign of composure giving way, as in a tearing rage or tearing fit.

clue.text: Seven minus one is _______!

indicators.note: minus one says a single letter is taken off the front of the number word

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A child's arithmetic exercise: seven take away one gives a number of a certain kind.
explanation.walkthrough: Both readings work: seven minus one is six, an even number, and the word seven minus one letter leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Six is divisible by two, making it an even number.

clue.text: Church worker's pouch is light brown, and red inside

indicators.note: inside says one piece is tucked in among the others

blocks.note: a sac is a pouch, as in biology
R is the usual abbreviation for red
taken as written
tan is a light brown colour

explanation.surface: A church employee's bag is tan on the outside with a red lining.
explanation.definitionFit: A sacristan is the officer who looks after a church's sacristy and its sacred vessels.

clue.text: Touched fabric

blocks.note: first meaning: past tense of feel, to handle
second meaning: a matted woollen cloth

explanation.walkthrough: Read together it sounds like stroking cloth; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both the past tense of the verb meaning to sense by hand and a pressed wool material.

clue.text: Generically keeping name

indicators.note: the long word keeps a shorter one held within its letters

blocks.note: a run of letters in the middle of the word

explanation.surface: A rule about holding on to a name only in a generic sense, as brands sometimes do.
explanation.walkthrough: Fittingly, Erica is also the generic name for heather, so the hiding word is apt.
explanation.definitionFit: Erica is a woman's first name, so it serves as an example of a name.

clue.text: Recklessly use up tome, absorbed by T.S. Eliot's stormy quality

indicators.note: doing something recklessly means without order, so these letters are scrambled
something absorbed by another is taken inside it

blocks.note: the poet's initials, used as letters
taken as written, then rearranged
Eliot Ness, the Prohibition agent who led the Untouchables

explanation.surface: Wasting a book on a poet's turbulent temperament.
explanation.walkthrough: T.S. Eliot's name is split: his initials wrap the jumbled letters, and Eliot is then read as Eliot Ness, the famous lawman.
explanation.definitionFit: Tempestuousness is the quality of being stormy, literally or in temperament.

clue.text: Joint action assumed unbroken

indicators.note: to assume is to take on, so the answer is taken on board within the words

blocks.note: the run of letters spanning the two words

explanation.surface: A co-operative effort is presumed to have stayed solid.
explanation.definitionFit: Something intact is whole and undamaged, which is what unbroken means.

clue.text: Creature you might find in Australia: dead ape

blocks.clueFragment: Creature you might find in Australia
blocks.note: the emu is a large flightless Australian bird
the late so-and-so is someone dead

explanation.surface: A wildlife spotter's list of Australian finds includes, oddly, a deceased primate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ape' looks like the animal at the end of a list of creatures, but it is a verb meaning copy.
explanation.definitionFit: To ape someone is to imitate them, which is what emulating means.

clue.text: Verify argument against a company

blocks.note: the cons are the arguments against, as in pros and cons
a firm is a company

explanation.surface: Someone checks the case being made against a business.
explanation.definitionFit: To confirm something is to establish that it is true, the same as verifying it.

clue.text: Tuna salad infested with Rhode Island rodent

indicators.note: a salad is a tossed mixture, so the letters are thrown together in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
RI is the postal abbreviation for Rhode Island

explanation.surface: A tuna salad turns out to be crawling with a vermin from Rhode Island.
explanation.definitionFit: The nutria, or coypu, is a large South American rodent now widespread in the US.

clue.text: Where some clergy live, a tabloid is taken in by wrongdoing

indicators.note: something taken in by another thing ends up sitting inside it

blocks.note: vice is wickedness
taken as written
a rag is a disparaging name for a low-grade newspaper

explanation.surface: In the parsonage, a scandal sheet gets caught up in someone's misconduct.
explanation.definitionFit: A vicarage is the house provided for a vicar, a parish priest.

clue.text: Actor is angry, flailing about in horse-drawn vehicle

indicators.note: flailing about is wild thrashing, so the letters are thrown into disorder
in places the rearranged letters inside the vehicle

blocks.note: a cart is pulled by a horse
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: An enraged performer thrashes around inside a horse-drawn wagon.
explanation.walkthrough: The angry flailing is the anagram, not the actor's mood; the answer is CARY GRANT.
explanation.definitionFit: Cary Grant was a leading Hollywood film star of the 1930s to 1960s.

clue.text: Look after confused admiral (or animal?)

indicators.note: a confused person's thoughts are jumbled, and so are these letters

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged
lo is an old word meaning look or behold

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to care for a muddled naval officer, who may be more beast than man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Look after' reads as care for, but here 'after' just places the second piece at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: The armadillo is an armoured burrowing mammal of the Americas.

clue.text: Bird repressing a cry of pain, namely…

indicators.note: to repress is to hold something down within, so one piece is held inside the other

blocks.note: the tit is a small songbird
ow is what you yell when hurt

explanation.surface: A bird stifles its yelp of pain, and the sentence runs on to introduce an example.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis ties this to the next clue, but the two answers are separate.
explanation.definitionFit: To wit is a formal phrase used to introduce a specification, exactly as namely does.

clue.text: SometWBg helpful for getting clean

blocks.note: surface reading: an aid to someone getting off drink or drugs, as in rehab
setter's reading: literally washing, so the thing is a bathroom fixture for washing hands and face

explanation.walkthrough: The published clue text is damaged: 'SometWBg' stands where 'Something' must have been printed. Read it as 'Something helpful for getting clean'; the phrase suggests recovery from addiction, but means plain washing.
explanation.definitionFit: A washbasin is a sink for washing your hands and face, so it literally helps you get clean.

clue.text: …a warning from Princess Irene

indicators.note: from says the letters are drawn straight out of the words that follow

blocks.note: the run of letters spanning the two words

explanation.surface: Continuing the last clue, a royal named Irene issues a caution.
explanation.definitionFit: A siren is an alarm that sounds a warning, as on an ambulance or air-raid tower.

clue.text: Sleep on relative's linen

blocks.note: a nap is a short sleep
kin are relatives

explanation.surface: Someone dozes off on a family member's bedsheets.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'on' means placed above, so the sleep comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: Table linen includes napkins, cloths for wiping the mouth at meals.

clue.text: Writing, as I foment trouble!

indicators.note: fomenting trouble means stirring things up, and the letters before it are stirred

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: An agitator boasts that their text is how they stir up unrest.
explanation.walkthrough: An &lit flavour: a manifesto is exactly the sort of writing that foments trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: A manifesto is a published written declaration of aims, a piece of writing.

clue.text: Musician: "FDR lied unconscionably"

indicators.note: acting unconscionably means without restraint or scruple, so the letters run wild

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A performer quoted accusing President Roosevelt of shameless lying.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiddler plays the violin, so is a kind of musician.

clue.text: Adventure in Space ruined by commercial exploitation, at first

indicators.note: something ruined is wrecked, so the word before it is knocked into a new shape
at first keeps just the opening letter of the word before it

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged
a commercial is an advertisement
the opening letter of exploitation

explanation.surface: A grumble that space exploration has been spoiled by commercial interests.
explanation.definitionFit: An escapade is a daring or reckless adventure.

clue.text: Following Clinton's lead, conceal reproach

indicators.note: a lead goes in front, so only the opening letter of the name is kept

blocks.note: the opening letter of the name
to hide is to conceal

explanation.surface: Taking a cue from Clinton, someone covers up a scolding.
explanation.definitionFit: To chide is to scold or reproach someone mildly.

clue.text: Bricks bother the elite, for the most part

indicators.note: for the most part means mostly, so all but the final letter is used

blocks.note: ado is fuss or bother
the best are the elite

explanation.surface: Building materials seem to irritate the upper class, mostly.
explanation.definitionFit: Adobes are sun-dried clay bricks, used in the American Southwest and Mexico.

clue.text: Fancy woman with that guy

blocks.note: W is the standard abbreviation for woman
him refers to that guy

explanation.surface: A kept woman, or mistress, is seen out with a certain man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy woman' reads as a lover; split them and 'Fancy' is a noun meaning a passing impulse.
explanation.definitionFit: A fancy, in the sense of a sudden notion or desire, is a whim.

clue.text: Insignificant four (or six) involved in experiment

indicators.note: something involved in another is wrapped up inside it

blocks.note: a trial is a test or experiment
Roman four; read the other way it is Roman six, as the bracket teases

explanation.surface: A tiny number of subjects, four or six, are deemed too few for a meaningful experiment.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracket is a joke: the Roman numeral for four reversed is the Roman numeral for six, and the answer reads either way inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Trivial means of little importance or value, so unimportant or insignificant.

clue.text: Location in Rome that's entirely water, we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the words are judged by their spoken sound rather than spelling

blocks.note: wholly means entirely
the sea is a body of water

explanation.surface: Somewhere in Rome is said to be completely underwater, like Venice.
explanation.definitionFit: The Holy See is the papal jurisdiction, seated in Vatican City within Rome.

clue.text: The Return of the King? Sounds like part of an old movie

indicators.note: sounds like tells us to go by how the name is spoken, not how it is spelt
a return goes back the way it came, so the letters are read from the end

blocks.note: Shakespeare's King Lear, written the way the name is spoken

explanation.surface: A title that evokes the Tolkien film, presented as one segment of an old picture.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that this is not the Tolkien film: the King is Lear, whose name is said like LEER, and returning that gives REEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Old films came on reels, spools of film each holding one section of the movie.

clue.text: Comes back to cut short the psychic distress of the post-war generation?

indicators.note: something cut short loses its end, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: a boomer is a baby boomer, born in the post-war birth surge
angst is anxiety or psychic distress

explanation.surface: Someone keeps returning to curtail their generation's anxieties.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the wordplay as boomer angst, the angst of the baby boomers, losing its final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that boomerangs returns to its source, as the thrown Australian weapon does.
